svg.title: Power Pages ALM inner loop: daily development cycle
svg.desc: Animated diagram showing the daily author, preview, validate, and commit cycle inside one developer environment.

g.text: Power Pages ALM — the inner loop up close
Environment strategy and branching: how multiple developers build the same feature in parallel without environment conflicts
An environment is a container for Dataverse, apps, flows and Pages — plus the permissions to use them.
commands are examples — Studio, VS Code or a pipeline does the same job
1 — Seed the baseline: build it once, in one place
The team builds the solution and the Power Pages site together in a shared integration environment, then commits that state to source control
Shared · team-owned · never the default environment
Baseline is built here once, then this environment
stays as the shared place to validate merged features.
2 · Unpack it into reviewable source files
3 · Download the code site as source
Solution and site land in the same commit.
The single source of truth across time,
Every branch carries solution/src/** and site/**.
Create one shared branch for the feature from
the latest integration baseline in develop.
Each developer creates a work branch from this
2 — Fan out: every developer gets their own branch and environment
Each developer follows the same four steps independently, then opens a pull request (PR) back to the shared feature integration branch
Developer work branches start here and merge back through PRs.
Works independently in an isolated environment.
Import the unmanaged solution built from this branch.
shown step by step in panel 3 below
Commit, then open a pull request.
Works independently in an isolated environment.
Import the unmanaged solution built from this branch.
shown step by step in panel 3 below
Commit, then open a pull request.
The same pattern, for every developer on the feature.
Import the unmanaged solution built from this branch.
shown step by step in panel 3 below
Commit, then open a pull request.
Before each new change: pull the shared feature integration branch, then re-import it into your Dev environment
3 — See the daily development loop up close
Inside their own environment a developer cycles here many times before opening a single pull request
Moving work between your Dev environment and Git
Pull the site down as code
e.g. pac solution export + pac solution unpack
Site source, web templates, Liquid, JS and CSS bundles, and the
unpacked solution all live in the same branch.
Nothing here is shared. Nobody else sees it until the pull request.
Local validation green · conventional commit written
One commit carries the site source and the unpacked solution
then push and open a pull request
4 — Guardrails keep the environment strategy reliable
Never share a Dev environment, and never build in the
default environment. Use per-user developer environments.
Definitions travel with the solution. Supply target-specific
values during import or through deployment settings.
Makers build unmanaged in Dev. Only managed artifacts
from the pipeline enter Test and Prod.
Agree the prefix and solution name in the integration
environment before anyone forks, or merges will fight.
Test and Prod — covered in deck 3
Source control is the single source of truth across time, versions and environments.
Next: the outer loop — branching strategy, CI/CD and how a release is cut →
